scoring_justification: Cannot recompute DFT energies; verify structural trends and thresholds against paper‑reported relationships.

hidden_assets.purpose: Structural thresholds derived from paper‑reported trends: W_sep pure ~0.009 J/m², Co/Ni/V C‑X >0.6, early TM Pt‑X >3.0, charge ratio Ti ~0.75, Co/Ni/V ~1.0.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper Figures and text: Fig.2, Fig.3b and discussion.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Extracted numeric thresholds from paper's stated inequalities and reported approximate values.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These thresholds reflect the paper's own findings; they are not arbitrary.

outputs.description: CSV file with columns: adatom (e.g., 'Co','Ni','V','Ti','None'), W_sep_Pt_X (float, J/m^2), W_sep_C_X (float, J/m^2).
CSV file with columns: adatom (str), charge_to_Pt (float, elementary charge units), charge_to_C (float, elementary charge units).

output_contract.notes: The hidden checker verifies relative trends: W_sep_Pt_X > W_sep_C_X for every adatom; for 'None' both W_sep values near zero; the maximum W_sep_C_X among Co, Ni, V is at least 0.4 J/m^2; charge transfer ratios and that Ti exhibits the highest W_sep_Pt_X and highest charge_to_Pt.

steps.description: Verify structural trends in work of separation: Pt-X > C-X, pure interface near zero, promising adatoms have high C-X, Ti has highest Pt-X.
Verify charge transfer structural trends: ratio thresholds for promising adatoms and Ti, Ti has highest charge to Pt.
